contradict_spans: The patient denied any trauma history and had no history of connective tissue disease nor any evidence of systemic involvement

candidates.name: Lichen planopilaris
support_spans: The patient reported that when the lesion had begun approximately 10 years earlier, he had received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
candidates.why: The patient's history of intralesional steroid injections and the presence of linear hair loss and hair thinning are consistent with lichen planopilaris.

candidates.name: Discoid lupus erythematosus
support_spans: Histopathologic examination revealed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
candidates.why: The histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis are consistent with the immune-mediated mechanism of discoid lupus erythematosus.

candidates.name: Lichen planopilaris
support_spans: Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
candidates.why: The dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation are consistent with the inflammatory mechanism of lichen planopilaris.

key_evidence_spans: A man in his 50s presented with an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
The patient reported that when the lesion had begun approximately 10 years earlier, he had received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex
Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
Histopathologic examination revealed predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
Direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels
The patient denied any trauma history and had no history of connective tissue disease nor any evidence of systemic involvement
